BitField.name: PDID
BitField.description:
Part Device Identification Number (Read Only)
This register reflects device part number code. Software can read this register to identify which device is used.

BitField.name: PORF
BitField.description:
POR Reset Flag
The POR reset flag is set by the 'Reset Signal' from the Power-on Reset (POR) Controller or bit CHIPRST (SYS_IPRST0[0]) to indicate the previous reset source.
Note: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.

Enum.description: No reset from POR or CHIPRST
Power-on Reset (POR) or CHIPRST had issued the reset signal to reset the system

BitField.name: PINRF
BitField.description:
NRESET Pin Reset Flag
The nRESET pin reset flag is set by the 'Reset Signal' from the nRESET Pin to indicate the previous reset source.
Note: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.

Enum.description: No reset from nRESET pin
Pin nRESET had issued the reset signal to reset the system

BitField.name: WDTRF
BitField.description:
WDT Reset Flag
The WDT reset flag is set by the 'Reset Signal' from the Watchdog Timer or Window Watchdog Timer to indicate the previous reset source.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: Watchdog Timer register RSTF(WDT_CTL[2]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WDT time-out reset. Window Watchdog Timer register WWDTRF(WWDT_STATUS[1]) bit is set if the system has been reset by WWDT time-out reset.

Enum.description: No reset from watchdog timer or window watchdog timer
The watchdog timer or window watchdog timer had issued the reset signal to reset the system

BitField.name: LVRF
BitField.description:
LVR Reset Flag
The LVR reset flag is set by the 'Reset Signal' from the Low Voltage Reset Controller to indicate the previous reset source.
Note: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.

Enum.description: No reset from LVR
LVR controller had issued the reset signal to reset the system

BitField.name: BODRF
BitField.description:
BOD Reset Flag
The BOD reset flag is set by the 'Reset Signal' from the Brown-Out Detector to indicate the previous reset source.
Note: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.

Enum.description: No reset from BOD
The BOD had issued the reset signal to reset the system

BitField.name: MCURF
BitField.description:
System Reset Flag
The system reset flag is set by the 'Reset Signal' from the Cortex-M4 Core to indicate the previous reset source.
Note: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.

Enum.description: No reset from Cortex-M4

The Cortex-M4 had issued the reset signal to reset the system by writing 1 to the bit SYSRESETREQ(AIRCR[2], Application Interrupt and Reset Control Register, address = 0xE000ED0C) in system control registers of Cortex-M4 core

BitField.name: HRESETRF
BitField.description:
HRESET Reset Flag
The HRESET reset flag is set by the 'Reset Signal' from the HRESET.
Note: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.

Enum.description: No reset from HRESET
Reset from HRESET

BitField.name: CPURF
BitField.description:
CPU Reset Flag
The CPU reset flag is set by hardware if software writes CPURST (SYS_IPRST0[1]) 1 to reset Cortex-M4 Core and Flash Memory Controller (FMC).
Note: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.

Enum.description: No reset from CPU
The Cortex-M4 Core and FMC are reset by software setting CPURST to 1

BitField.name: CPULKRF
BitField.description:
CPU Lockup Reset Flag
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.
Note 2: When CPU lockup happened under ICE is connected, this flag will set to 1 but chip will not reset.

Enum.description: No reset from CPU lockup happened
The Cortex-M4 lockup happened and chip is reset

BitField.name: CHIPRST
BitField.description:
Chip One-shot Reset (Write Protect)
Setting this bit will reset the whole chip, including Processor core and all peripherals, and this bit will automatically return to 0 after the 2 clock cycles.
The CHIPRST is same as the POR reset, all the chip controllers is reset and the chip setting from Flash are also reload.
About the difference between CHIPRST and SYSRESETREQ(AIRCR[2]), please refer to section 7.2.2
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Chip normal operation
Chip one-shot reset

BitField.name: CPURST
BitField.description:
Processor Core One-shot Reset (Write Protect)
Setting this bit will only reset the processor core and Flash Memory Controller(FMC), and this bit will automatically return to 0 after the 2 clock cycles.
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Processor core normal operation
Processor core one-shot reset

BitField.name: PDMA0RST

BitField.name: BODEN
BitField.description:
Brown-out Detector Enable Bit (Write Protect)
The default value is set by Flash controller user configuration register CBODEN (CONFIG0 [19]).
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Brown-out Detector function Disabled
Brown-out Detector function Enabled

BitField.name: BODRSTEN
BitField.description:
Brown-out Reset Enable Bit (Write Protect)
The default value is set by Flash controller user configuration register CBORST(CONFIG0[20]) bit.
Note 1: While the Brown-out Detector function is enabled (BODEN high) and BOD reset function is enabled (BODRSTEN high), BOD will assert a signal to reset chip when the detected voltage is lower than the threshold (BODOUT high).
While the BOD function is enabled (BODEN high) and BOD interrupt function is enabled (BODRSTEN low), BOD will assert an interrupt if BODOUT is high. BOD interrupt will keep till to the BODEN set to 0. BOD interrupt can be blocked by disabling the NVIC BOD interrupt or disabling BOD function (set BODEN low).
Note 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Brown-out 'INTERRUPT' function Enabled
Brown-out 'RESET' function Enabled

BitField.name: BODIF
BitField.description:
Brown-out Detector Interrupt Flag
Note: Write 1 to clear this bit to 0.

Enum.description: Brown-out Detector does not detect any voltage draft at VDD down through or up through the voltage of BODVL setting

When Brown-out Detector detects the VDD is dropped down through the voltage of BODVL setting or the VDD is raised up through the voltage of BODVL setting, this bit is set to 1 and the brown-out interrupt is requested if brown-out interrupt is enabled

BitField.name: BODLPM
BitField.description:
Brown-out Detector Low Power Mode (Write Protect)
Note 1: The BOD consumes about 100uA in normal mode, the low power mode can reduce the current to about 1/10 but slow the BOD response.
Note 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: BOD operate in normal mode (default)
BOD Low Power mode Enabled

BitField.name: BODOUT
BitField.description:
Brown-out Detector Output Status
It means the detected voltage is lower than BODVL setting. If the BODEN is 0, BOD function disabled, this bit always responds 0000.

Enum.description: Brown-out Detector output status is 0
Brown-out Detector output status is 1

BitField.name: LVREN
BitField.description:
Low Voltage Reset Enable Bit (Write Protect)
The LVR function resets the chip when the input power voltage is lower than LVR circuit setting. LVR function is enabled by default.
Note 1: After enabling the bit, the LVR function will be active with 100us delay for LVR output stable (default).
Note 2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Low Voltage Reset function Disabled
Low Voltage Reset function Enabled

BitField.name: BODDGSEL
BitField.description:
Brown-out Detector Output De-glitch Time Select (Write Protect)
Note: These bits are write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: BOD output is sampled by RC10K clock
4 system clock (HCLK)
8 system clock (HCLK)
16 system clock (HCLK)
32 system clock (HCLK)
64 system clock (HCLK)
128 system clock (HCLK)
256 system clock (HCLK)

BitField.name: LVRDGSEL
BitField.description:
LVR Output De-glitch Time Select (Write Protect)
Note: These bits are write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Without de-glitch function
4 system clock (HCLK)
8 system clock (HCLK)
16 system clock (HCLK)
32 system clock (HCLK)
64 system clock (HCLK)
128 system clock (HCLK)
256 system clock (HCLK)

BitField.name: LVRRDY
BitField.description:
Low Voltage Reset Ready Flag (Read Only)
When the LVR function first enable, need more HCLK to wait LVR ready.

Enum.description: Low Voltage Reset function Disabled
Low Voltage Reset function Enabled

Brown-out Detector Threshold Voltage Selection (Write Protect)
The default value is set by Flash controller user configuration register CBOV (CONFIG0 [23:21]).
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Brown-Out Detector threshold voltage is 1.6V
Brown-Out Detector threshold voltage is 1.8V
Brown-Out Detector threshold voltage is 2.0V
Brown-Out Detector threshold voltage is 2.2V
Brown-Out Detector threshold voltage is 2.4V
Brown-Out Detector threshold voltage is 2.6V
Brown-Out Detector threshold voltage is 2.8V
Brown-Out Detector threshold voltage is 3.0V

BitField.name: FREQSEL
BitField.description:
Trim Frequency Selection
This field indicates the target frequency of 48 MHz internal high speed RC oscillator (HIRC) auto trim.
During auto trim operation, if clock error detected with CESTOPEN is set to 1 or trim retry limitation count reached, this field will be cleared to 00 automatically.

Enum.description: Disable HIRC auto trim function
Enable HIRC auto trim function and trim HIRC to 48 MHz

BitField.name: LOOPSEL
BitField.description:
Trim Calculation Loop Selection
This field defines that trim value calculation is based on how many reference clocks.
Note: For example, if LOOPSEL is set as 00, auto trim circuit will calculate trim value based on the average frequency difference in 4 clocks of reference clock.

Enum.description: Trim value calculation is based on average difference in 4 clocks of reference clock
Trim value calculation is based on average difference in 8 clocks of reference clock
Trim value calculation is based on average difference in 16 clocks of reference clock
Trim value calculation is based on average difference in 32 clocks of reference clock

BitField.name: RETRYCNT
BitField.description:
Trim Value Update Limitation Count
This field defines that how many times the auto trim circuit will try to update the HIRC trim value before the frequency of HIRC locked.
Once the HIRC locked, the internal trim value update counter will be reset.
If the trim value update counter reached this limitation value and frequency of HIRC still doesn't lock, the auto trim operation will be disabled and FREQSEL will be cleared to 00.

Enum.description: Trim retry count limitation is 64 loops
Trim retry count limitation is 128 loops
Trim retry count limitation is 256 loops
Trim retry count limitation is 512 loops

BitField.name: CESTOPEN
BitField.description: Clock Error Stop Enable Bit

Enum.description: The trim operation is keep going if clock is inaccuracy
The trim operation is stopped if clock is inaccuracy

BitField.name: BOUNDEN
BitField.description: Boundary Enable Bit

Enum.description: Boundary function Disabled
Boundary function Enabled

BitField.name: REFCKSEL
BitField.description:
Reference Clock Selection
Note: HIRC trim reference clock is 20 kHz in test mode.

Enum.description: HIRC trim reference clock is from LXT (32.768 kHz)
HIRC trim reference clock is from internal USB synchronous mode

BitField.name: BOUNDARY
BitField.description:
Boundary Selection
Fill the boundary range from 0x1 to 0x31, 0x0 is reserved.
Note: This field is effective only when the BOUNDEN(SYS_HIRCTRIMCTL[9]) is enabled.

BitField.name: TFAILIEN
BitField.description:
Trim Failure Interrupt Enable Bit
This bit controls if an interrupt will be triggered while HIRC trim value update limitation count reached and HIRC frequency still not locked on target frequency set by FREQSEL(SYS_IRCTCTL[1:0]).
If this bit is high and TFAILIF(SYS_IRCTISTS[1]) is set during auto trim operation, an interrupt will be triggered to notify that HIRC trim value update limitation count was reached.

Enum.description: Disable TFAILIF(SYS_IRCTISTS[1]) status to trigger an interrupt to CPU
Enable TFAILIF(SYS_IRCTISTS[1]) status to trigger an interrupt to CPU

BitField.name: CLKEIEN
BitField.description:
Clock Error Interrupt Enable Bit
This bit controls if CPU would get an interrupt while clock is inaccuracy during auto trim operation.
If this bit is set to1, and CLKERRIF(SYS_IRCTISTS[2]) is set during auto trim operation, an interrupt will be triggered to notify the clock frequency is inaccuracy.

Enum.description: Disable CLKERRIF(SYS_IRCTISTS[2]) status to trigger an interrupt to CPU
Enable CLKERRIF(SYS_IRCTISTS[2]) status to trigger an interrupt to CPU

BitField.name: FREQLOCK
BitField.description:
HIRC Frequency Lock Status
This bit indicates the HIRC frequency is locked.
This is a status bit and doesn't trigger any interrupt
Write 1 to clear this to 0. This bit will be set automatically, if the frequency is lock and the RC_TRIM is enabled.

Enum.description: The internal high-speed oscillator frequency doesn't lock at 48 MHz yet
The internal high-speed oscillator frequency locked at 48 MHz

BitField.name: TFAILIF
BitField.description:
Trim Failure Interrupt Status
This bit indicates that HIRC trim value update limitation count reached and the HIRC clock frequency still doesn't be locked. Once this bit is set, the auto trim operation stopped and FREQSEL(SYS_IRCTCTL[1:0]) will be cleared to 00 by hardware automatically.
If this bit is set and TFAILIEN(SYS_IRCTIEN[1]) is high, an interrupt will be triggered to notify that HIRC trim value update limitation count was reached. Write 1 to clear this to 0.

Enum.description: Trim value update limitation count does not reach
Trim value update limitation count reached and HIRC frequency still not locked

BitField.name: CLKERRIF
BitField.description:
Clock Error Interrupt Status
When the frequency of 32.768 kHz external low speed crystal oscillator (LXT) or 48 MHz internal high speed RC oscillator (HIRC) is shift larger to unreasonable value, this bit will be set and to be an indicate that clock frequency is inaccuracy
Once this bit is set to 1, the auto trim operation stopped and FREQSEL(SYS_IRCTCL[1:0]) will be cleared to 00 by hardware automatically if CESTOPEN(SYS_IRCTCTL[8]) is set to 1.
If this bit is set and CLKEIEN(SYS_IRCTIEN[2]) is high, an interrupt will be triggered to notify the clock frequency is inaccuracy. Write 1 to clear this to 0.

Enum.description: Clock frequency is accuracy
Clock frequency is inaccuracy

BitField.name: OVBDIF
BitField.description:
Over Boundary Status
When the over boundary function is set, if there occurs the over boundary condition, this flag will be set.
Note 1: Write 1 to clear this flag.

Enum.description: Over boundary coundition did not occur
Over boundary coundition occurred

BitField.name: REGLCTL
BitField.description:
Register Lock Control Code
Some registers have write-protection function. Writing these registers have to disable the protected function by writing the sequence value '59h', '16h', '88h' to this field. After this sequence is completed, the REGLCTL bit will be set to 1 and write-protection registers can be normal write.

REGLCTL[0]
Register Lock Control Disable Index

Enum.description: Write-protection Enabled for writing protected registers. Any write to the protected register is ignored
Write-protection Disabled for writing protected registers

BitField.name: POROFFAN
BitField.description:
Power-on Reset Enable Bit (Write Protect)
After powered on, User can turn off internal analog POR circuit to save power by writing 0x5AA5 to this field.
The analog POR circuit will be active again when this field is set to another value or chip is reset by other reset source, including:
nRESET, Watchdog, LVR reset, BOD reset, ICE reset command and the software-chip reset function.
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
Note: M48xID/M487KMCAN series will disable POR by hardware when system enter power-down mode.

BitField.name: ENABLE
BitField.description: System Tick Counter Enabled

Enum.description: Counter Disabled
Counter will operate in a multi-shot manner

BitField.name: TICKINT
BitField.description: System Tick Interrupt Enabled

Enum.description: Counting down to 0 does not cause the SysTick exception to be pended. Software can use COUNTFLAG to determine if a count to zero has occurred
Counting down to 0 will cause the SysTick exception to be pended. Clearing the SysTick current value register by a register write in software will not cause SysTick to be pended

BitField.name: CLKSRC
BitField.description: System Tick Clock Source Selection

Enum.description: Clock source is the (optional) external reference clock
Core clock used for SysTick

BitField.name: COUNTFLAG
BitField.description:
System Tick Counter Flag
Returns 1 if timer counted to 0 since last time this register was read.
COUNTFLAG is set by a count transition from 1 to 0.
COUNTFLAG is cleared on read or by a write to the Current Value register.

BitField.name: RELOAD
BitField.description:
System Tick Reload Value
Value to load into the Current Value register when the counter reaches 0.

BitField.name: CURRENT
BitField.description:
System Tick Current Value
Current counter value. This is the value of the counter at the time it is sampled. The counter does not provide read-modify-write protection. The register is write-clear. A software write of any value will clear the register to 0.

BitField.name: VECTACTIVE
BitField.description: Number of the Current Active Exception

Enum.description: Thread mode

BitField.name: RETTOBASE
BitField.description:
Preempted Active Exceptions Indicator
Indicate whether There are Preempted Active Exceptions

Enum.description: there are preempted active exceptions to execute
there are no active exceptions, or the currently-executing exception is the only active exception

BitField.name: VECTPENDING
BitField.description:
Number of the Highest Pended Exception
Indicate the Exception Number of the Highest Priority Pending Enabled Exception
The value indicated by this field includes the effect of the BASEPRI and FAULTMASK registers, but not any effect of the PRIMASK register.

Enum.description: No pending exceptions

BitField.name: ISRPENDING
BitField.description: Interrupt Pending Flag, Excluding NMI and Faults (Read Only)

Enum.description: Interrupt not pending
Interrupt pending

BitField.name: ISRPREEMPT
BitField.description:
Interrupt Preempt Bit (Read Only)
If set, a pending exception will be serviced on exit from the debug halt state.

BitField.name: PENDSTRTC_CAL
BitField.description:
SysTick Exception Clear-pending Bit
Write Operation:
Note: This is a write only bit. To clear the PENDST bit, you must 'write 0 to PENDSTSET and write 1 to PENDSTRTC_CAL' at the same time.

Enum.description: No effect
Remove the pending state from the SysTick exception

BitField.name: PENDSTSET
BitField.description:
SysTick Exception Set-pending Bit
Write Operation:

Enum.description:
No effect.
SysTick exception is not pending

Change SysTick exception state to pending.
SysTick exception is pending

BitField.name: PENDSVRTC_CAL
BitField.description:
PendSV Clear-pending Bit
Write Operation:
Note: This is a write only bit. To clear the PENDSV bit, you must 'write 0 to PENDSVSET and write 1 to PENDSVRTC_CAL' at the same time.

Enum.description: No effect
Remove the pending state from the PendSV exception

BitField.name: PENDSVSET
BitField.description:
PendSV Set-pending Bit
Write Operation:
Note: Writing 1 to this bit is the only way to set the PendSV exception state to pending.

Enum.description:
No effect.
PendSV exception is not pending

Change PendSV exception state to pending.
PendSV exception is pending

BitField.name: NMIPENDSET
BitField.description:
NMI Set-pending Bit
Write Operation:
Note: Because NMI is the highest-priority exception, normally the processor enters the NMI exception handler as soon as it detects a write of 1 to this bit. Entering the handler then clears this bit to 0. This means a read of this bit by the NMI exception handler returns 1 only if the NMI signal is reasserted while the processor is executing that handler.

Enum.description:
No effect.
NMI exception is not pending

Change NMI exception state to pending.
NMI exception is pending

Register.name: AIRCR
Register.description: Application Interrupt and Reset Control Register

BitField.name: VECTCLRACTIVE
BitField.description:
Exception Active Status Clear Bit
Setting This Bit To 1 Will Clears All Active State Information For Fixed And Configurable Exceptions
This bit is write only and can only be written when the core is halted.
Note: It is the debugger's responsibility to re-initialize the stack.

BitField.name: SYSRESETREQ
BitField.description:
System Reset Request
Writing This Bit to 1 Will Cause A Reset Signal To Be Asserted To The Chip And Indicate A Reset Is Requested
This bit is write only and self-cleared as part of the reset sequence.

BitField.name: PRIGROUP
BitField.description:
Interrupt Priority Grouping
This field determines the Split Of Group priority from subpriority,

BitField.name: ENDIANNESS
BitField.description: Data Endianness

BitField.name: VECTORKEY
BitField.description:
Register Access Key
When writing this register, this field should be 0x05FA, otherwise the write action will be unpredictable.
The VECTORKEY filed is used to prevent accidental write to this register from resetting the system or clearing of the exception status.

BitField.name: SLEEPONEXIT
BitField.description:
Sleep-on-exit Enable Control
This bit indicate Sleep-On-Exit when Returning from Handler Mode to Thread Mode.
Setting this bit to 1 enables an interrupt driven application to avoid returning to an empty main application.

Enum.description: Do not sleep when returning to Thread mode
Enter sleep, or deep sleep, on return from an ISR to Thread mode

BitField.name: SLEEPDEEP
BitField.description:
Processor Deep Sleep and Sleep Mode Selection
Control whether the Processor Uses Sleep Or Deep Sleep as its Low Power Mode.

Enum.description: Deep sleep

BitField.name: SEVONPEND
BitField.description:
Send Event on Pending
When an event or interrupt enters pending state, the event signal wakes up the processor from WFE. If the processor is not waiting for an event, the event is registered and affects the next WFE.
The processor also wakes up on execution of an SEV instruction or an external event.

Enum.description: Only enabled interrupts or events can wake up the processor, while disabled interrupts are excluded
Enabled events and all interrupts, including disabled interrupts, can wake up the processor

BitField.name: PRI_4

BitField.name: PRI_11
BitField.description:
Priority of System Handler 11 - SVCall
'0' denotes the highest priority and '3' denotes the lowest priority.

BitField.name: PRI_14
BitField.description:
Priority of System Handler 14 - PendSV
'0' denotes the highest priority and '3' denotes the lowest priority.

BitField.name: PRI_15
BitField.description:
Priority of System Handler 15 - SysTick
'0' denotes the highest priority and '3' denotes the lowest priority.

BitField.name: INTID
BitField.description:
Interrupt ID
Write to the STIR To Generate An Interrupt from Software
When the USERSETMPEND bit in the SCR is set to 1, unprivileged software can access the STIR
Interrupt ID of the interrupt to trigger, in the range 0-63. For example, a value of 0x03 specifies interrupt IRQ3.

Register.name: AHBMCTL
Register.description: AHB Bus Matrix Priority Control Register

BitField.name: INTACTEN
BitField.description:
Highest AHB Bus Priority of Cortex®-M4 Core Enable Bit (Write Protect)
Enable Cortex®-M4 Core With Highest AHB Bus Priority In AHB Bus Matrix
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Run robin mode
Cortex®-M4 CPU with highest bus priority when interrupt occusr

BitField.name: HXTEN
BitField.description:
HXT Enable Bit (Write Protect)
The bit default value is set by Flash controller user configuration register CONFIG0 [26:24]. When the default clock source is from HXT, this bit is set to 1 automatically.
Note: 1.This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
2.When HXT is enabled, GPIO must be set as input mode.

Enum.description: 4~24 MHz external high speed crystal (HXT) Disabled
4~24 MHz external high speed crystal (HXT) Enabled

BitField.name: LXTEN
BitField.description:
LXT Enable Bit (Write Protect)
Note: 1. This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
2. When LXT is enabled, GPIO must be set as input mode.

Enum.description: 32.768 kHz external low speed crystal (LXT) Disabled
32.768 kHz external low speed crystal (LXT) Enabled

BitField.name: HIRCEN
BitField.description:
HIRC Enable Bit (Write Protect)
Note:1.This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: 12 MHz internal high speed RC oscillator (HIRC) Disabled
12 MHz internal high speed RC oscillator (HIRC) Enabled

BitField.name: LIRCEN
BitField.description:

Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.description:
Enable the Wake-up Delay Counter (Write Protect)
When the chip wakes up from Power-down mode, the clock control will delay certain clock cycles to wait system clock stable.
The delayed clock cycle is 4096 clock cycles when chip works at 4~24 MHz external high speed crystal oscillator (HXT), and 256 clock cycles when chip works at 12 MHz internal high speed RC oscillator (HIRC).
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register

Enum.description: Clock cycles delay Disabled
Clock cycles delay Enabled

BitField.name: PDWKIEN
BitField.description:
Power-down Mode Wake-up Interrupt Enable Bit (Write Protect)
Note1: The interrupt will occur when both PDWKIF and PDWKIEN are high.
Note2: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Power-down mode wake-up interrupt Disabled
Power-down mode wake-up interrupt Enabled

BitField.name: PDWKIF
BitField.description:
Power-down Mode Wake-up Interrupt Status
Set by 'Power-down wake-up event', it indicates that resume from Power-down mode'
The flag is set if any wake-up source is occurred. Refer Power Modes and Wake-up Sources chapter.
Note1: Write 1 to clear the bit to 0.
Note2: This bit works only if PDWKIEN (CLK_PWRCTL[5]) set to 1.

BitField.name: PDEN
BitField.description:
System Power-down Enable (Write Protect)
When this bit is set to 1, Power-down mode is enabled and chip keeps active till the CPU sleep mode is also active and then the chip enters Power-down mode.
When chip wakes up from Power-down mode, this bit is auto cleared. Users need to set this bit again for next Power-down.
In Power-down mode, HXT and the HIRC will be disabled in this mode, but LXT and LIRC are not controlled by Power-down mode.
In Power-down mode, the PLL and system clock are disabled, and ignored the clock source selection. The clocks of peripheral are not controlled by Power-down mode, if the peripheral clock source is from LXT or LIRC.
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Chip will not enter Power-down mode after CPU sleep command WFI
Chip enters Power-down mode after CPU sleep command WFI

BitField.name: HXTGAIN
BitField.description:
HXT Gain Control Bit (Write Protect)
This is a protected register. Please refer to open lock sequence to program it.
Gain control is used to enlarge the gain of crystal to make sure crystal work normally. If gain control is enabled, crystal will consume more power than gain control off.
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: HXT frequency is lower than from 8 MHz
HXT frequency is from 8 MHz to 12 MHz
HXT frequency is from 12 MHz to 16 MHz
HXT frequency is higher than 16 MHz

BitField.name: PINWK0

This flag indicates that wake-up of chip from Deep Power-down mode was requested by a transition of the WAKEUP pin (GPC.0). This flag is cleared when DPD mode is entered.

BitField.name: RTCWK
BitField.description:

BitField.name: DBEN
BitField.description:

If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the wake-up. BitField.name: IOHR
BitField.description:
GPIO Hold Release
When GPIO enters deep power-down mode or standby power-down mode, all I/O status are hold to keep normal operating status. After chip was waked up from deep power-down mode or standby power-down mode, the I/O are still keep hold status until user set this bit to release I/O hold status.
Note: This bit is auto cleared by hardware.

BitField.name: TRNGEN
BitField.description:
Random Number Generator Enable Bit
This bit can be set to 1 only after ACT (TRNG_ACT[7]) bit is set to 1 and READY (TRNG_CTL[7]) bit became 1.
Note: TRNGEN is an enable bit of digital part. When TRNG is not required to generate random number, TRNGEN bit and ACT (TRNG_ACT[7]) bit should be set to 0 to reduce power consumption.

Enum.description: TRNG Disabled
TRNG Enabled

BitField.name: DVIF
BitField.description:
Data Valid (Read Only)
Note: This bit is cleared to '0' by reading TRNG_DATA.

Enum.description: Data is not valid. Reading from RNGD returns 0x00000000
Data is valid. A valid random number can be read form DATA(TRNG_DATA[7:0])

BitField.name: CLKPSC
BitField.description:
Clock Prescaler
The CLKPSC is the peripheral clock frequency range for the selected value , the CLKPSC setting must be higher than or equal to the actual peripheral clock frequency (for correct random bit generation). To change the CLKPSC setting, set TRNGEN bit to 0, change CLKPSC, and set TRNGEN bit to 1 to re-enable the TRNG.

Enum.description: 9 ~12 MHz
7 ~9 MHz
6 ~7 MHz
5 ~6 MHz
4 ~5 MHz

BitField.name: DVIEN
BitField.description: Data Valid Interrupt Enable Bit

Enum.description: Interrupt Disabled
Interrupt Enabled

BitField.name: READY
BitField.description:
Random Number Generator Ready (Read Only)
After ACT (TRNG_ACT[7]) bit is set, the READY bit become to 1 after a delay of 90us~120us.

Enum.description: RNG is not ready or activated
RNG is ready to be enabled

BitField.name: DATA
BitField.description:
Random Number Generator Data (Read Only)
The DATA store the random number is generated by TRNG and can be read only once.

BitField.name: ACT
BitField.description:
Random Number Generator Activation
After enable the ACT bit, it will active the TRNG module and wait the READY (TRNG_CTL[7]) bit to become 1.
Note: ACT is an enable bit of analog part. When TRNG is not required to generate random number, TRNGEN (TRNG_CTL[0]) bit and ACT bit should be set to 0 to reduce power consumption.

Enum.description: TRNG inactive
TRNG active

Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.name: BS
BitField.description:
Boot Select (Write Protect)
When MBS in CONFIG0 is 1, set/clear this bit to select next booting from LDROM/APROM, respectively. This bit also functions as chip booting status flag, which can be used to check where chip booted from. This bit is initiated with the inversed value of CBS[1] (CONFIG0[7]) after any reset is happened except CPU reset (CPU is 1) or system reset (SYS) is happened
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Boot from APROM when MBS (CONFIG0[5]) is 1
Boot from LDROM when MBS (CONFIG0[5]) is 1

BitField.name: APUEN
BitField.description:
APROM Update Enable Bit (Write Protect)
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: APROM cannot be updated when the chip runs in APROM
APROM can be updated when the chip runs in APROM

BitField.name: CFGUEN
BitField.description:
CONFIG Update Enable Bit (Write Protect)
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: CONFIG cannot be updated
CONFIG can be updated

BitField.name: LDUEN
BitField.description:
LDROM Update Enable Bit (Write Protect)
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: LDROM cannot be updated
LDROM can be updated

BitField.name: ISPFF
BitField.description:
ISP Fail Flag (Write Protect)
This bit is set by hardware when a triggered ISP meets any of the following conditions:
This bit needs to be cleared by writing 1 to it.
APROM writes to itself if APUEN is set to 0.
APROM(except for Data Flash) is erased/programmed if KEYLOCK is 1
LDROM writes to itself if LDUEN is set to 0.
LDROM is erased/programmed if KEYLOCK is set to 1
CONFIG is erased/programmed if CFGUEN is set to 0.
CONFIG is erased/programmed if KEYLOCK is set to 1 and KEYENROM[1:0] are 1
KPROM is erased/programmed if KEYLOCK is set to 1
Erase or Program command at brown-out detected
Destination address is illegal, such as over an available range.
Invalid ISP commands
Page Erase command at LOCK mode with ICE connection
Invalid operations (except for chip erase) with ICE connection if SBLOCK is not 0x5A
Read any content of boot loader with ICE connection
The base and size of new XOM regsions is wrong, overlap or writed twice
The input setting of XOM page erase function is wrong
The active XOM regsion is accessed (except for chip erase, page erase, chksum and read CID/DID)
The XOM setting page is accessed (except for chip erase, word program and read)
Violate the load code read protection
OTP is erased, multi-word programed or 64-bit read
Checksum or Flash All One Verification is not executed in their valid range
Block erase or bank erase is not executed in APROM
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.name: BL
BitField.description:
Boot Loader Booting (Write Protect)
This bit is initiated with the inversed value of MBS (CONFIG0[5]). Any reset, except CPU reset (CPU is 1) or system reset (SYS), BL will be reloaded. This bit is used to check chip boot from Boot Loader or not. User should keep original value of this bit when updating FMC_ISPCTL register.
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Boot from APROM or LDROM
Boot from Boot Loader

BitField.name: ISPADDR
BitField.description:
ISP Address
The M480 series is equipped with embedded Flash. ISPADDR[1:0] must be kept 00 for ISP 32-bit operation. ISPADDR[2:0] must be kept 000 for ISP 64-bit operation.
For CRC32 Checksum Calculation command, this field is the Flash starting address for checksum calculation, 4 Kbytes alignment is necessary for CRC32 checksum calculation.
For Flash32-bit Program, ISP address needs word alignment (4-byte). For Flash 64-bit Program, ISP address needs double word alignment (8-byte).

BitField.name: ISPDAT
BitField.description:
ISP Data
Write data to this register before ISP program operation.
Read data from this register after ISP read operation.

BitField.name: CMD
BitField.description:
ISP Command
ISP command table is shown below:
The other commands are invalid.

Enum.description: FLASH Read
Read Unique ID
Read Flash All-One Result
Read Company ID
Read Device ID
Read Checksum
FLASH 32-bit Program
FLASH Page Erase. Erase any page in two banks, except for OTP
FLASH Bank Erase. Erase all pages of APROM in BANK0 or BANK1
FLASH Block Erase. Erase four pages alignment of APROM in BANK0 or BANK1
FLASH Multi-Word Program
Run Flash All-One Verification
Run Checksum Calculation
Vector Remap
FLASH 64-bit Read
FLASH 64-bit Program

BitField.name: ISPGO
BitField.description:
ISP Start Trigger (Write Protect)
Write 1 to start ISP operation and this bit will be cleared to 0 by hardware automatically when ISP operation is finished.
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: ISP operation is finished
ISP is progressed

BitField.name: DFBA
BitField.description:
Data Flash Base Address
This register indicates Data Flash start address. It is a read only register.
The Data Flash is shared with APROM. the content of this register is loaded from CONFIG1

BitField.name: CACHEINV
BitField.description:
Flash Cache Invalidation (Write Protect)
Note 1: Write 1 to start cache invalidation. The value will be changed to 0 once the process finishes.
Note 2: This bit is write-protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.
Note 3: When ISP is processed, the Flash Cache will be invalid.

Enum.description: Flash Cache Invalidation finished (default)
Flash Cache Invalidation

BitField.name: ISPBUSY
BitField.description:
ISP Busy Flag (Read Only)
Write 1 to start ISP operation and this bit will be cleared to 0 by hardware automatically when ISP operation is finished.
This bit is the mirror of ISPGO(FMC_ISPTRG[0]).

Enum.description: ISP operation is finished
ISP is progressed

BitField.name: CBS
BitField.description:
Boot Selection of CONFIG (Read Only)
This bit is initiated with the CBS (CONFIG0[7:6]) after any reset is happened except CPU reset (CPU is 1) or system reset (SYS) is happened.

Enum.description: LDROM with IAP mode
LDROM without IAP mode
APROM with IAP mode
APROM without IAP mode

BitField.name: MBS
BitField.description:
Boot From Boot Loader Selection Flag (Read Only)
This bit is initiated with the MBS (CONFIG0[5]) after any reset is happened except CPU reset (CPU is 1) or system reset (SYS) is happened.

Enum.description: Boot from Boot Loader
Boot from LDROM/APROM.(.see CBS bit setting)

BitField.name: FCYCDIS
BitField.description:
Flash Access Cycle Auto-tuning Disable Flag (Read Only)
This bit is set if Flash access cycle auto-tunning function is disabled. The auto-tunning function is disabled by FADIS(FMC_CYCCTL[8]) or HIRC clock is not ready.

Enum.description: Flash access cycle auto-tuning Enabled
Flash access cyle auto-tuning Disabled

BitField.name: PGFF
BitField.description:
Flash Program with Fast Verification Flag (Read Only)
This bit is set if data is mismatched at ISP programming verification. This bit is clear by performing ISP Flash erase or ISP read CID operation

Enum.description: Flash Program is success
Flash Program is fail. Program data is different with data in the Flash memory

BitField.name: ISPFF
BitField.description:
ISP Fail Flag (Write Protect)
This bit is the mirror of ISPFF (FMC_ISPCTL[6]), it needs to be cleared by writing 1 to FMC_ISPCTL[6] or FMC_ISPSTS[6]. This bit is set by hardware when a triggered ISP meets any of the following conditions:
APROM writes to itself if APUEN is set to 0.
APROM(except for Data Flash) is erased/programmed if KEYLOCK is 1
LDROM writes to itself if LDUEN is set to 0.
LDROM is erased/programmed if KEYLOCK is set to 1
CONFIG is erased/programmed if CFGUEN is set to 0.
CONFIG is erased/programmed if KEYLOCK is set to 1 and KEYENROM[1:0] are 1
KPROM is erased/programmed if KEYLOCK is set to 1
Erase or Program command at brown-out detected
Destination address is illegal, such as over an available range.
Invalid ISP commands
Page Erase command at LOCK mode with ICE connection
Invalid operations (except for chip erase) with ICE connection if SBLOCK is not 0x5A
Read any content of boot loader with ICE connection
The base and size of new XOM regsions is wrong, overlap or writed twice
The input setting of XOM page erase function is wrong
The active XOM regsion is accessed (except for chip erase, page erase, chksum and read CID/DID)
The XOM setting page is accessed (except for chip erase, word program and read)
Violate the load code read protection
OTP is erased, multi-word programed or 64-bit read
Checksum or Flash All One Verification is not executed in their valid range
Block erase or bank erase is not executed in APROM
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

BitField.name: ALLONE
BitField.description:
Flash All-one Verification Flag
This bit is set by hardware if all of Flash bits are 1, and clear if Flash bits are not all 1 after 'Run Flash All-One Verification' complete; this bit also can be clear by writing 1

Enum.description: All of Flash bits are 1 after 'Run Flash All-One Verification' complete
Flash bits are not all 1 after 'Run Flash All-One Verification' complete

BitField.name: VECMAP
BitField.description:
Vector Page Mapping Address (Read Only)
All access to 0x0000_0000~0x0000_01FF is remapped to the Flash memory address {VECMAP[14:0], 9'h000} ~ {VECMAP[14:0], 9'h1FF}

BitField.name: CYCLE
BitField.description:
Flash Access Cycle Control (Write Protect)
This register is updated automatically by hardware while FCYCDIS (FMC_ISPSTS[4]) is 0, and updated by software while auto-tuning function disabled ( FADIS (FMC_CYCTL[8]) is 1)
The optimized HCLK working frequency range is 192 MHz
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: CPU access with zero wait cycle ; Flash access cycle is 1;
CPU access with one wait cycle if cache miss; Flash access cycle is 1;
CPU access with two wait cycles if cache miss; Flash access cycle is 2;
CPU access with three wait cycles if cache miss; Flash access cycle is 3;
CPU access with four wait cycles if cache miss; Flash access cycle is 4;
CPU access with five wait cycles if cache miss; Flash access cycle is 5;
CPU access with six wait cycles if cache miss; Flash access cycle is 6;
CPU access with seven wait cycles if cache miss; Flash access cycle is 7;
CPU access with eight wait cycles if cache miss; Flash access cycle is 8;

BitField.name: FADIS
BitField.description:
Flash Access Cycle Auto-tuning Disable Bit (Write Protect)
Set this bit to disable Flash access cycle auto-tuning function
Note: This bit is write protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register. When FMC is doing auto-tuning, we considered as an ISP operation need to monitor busy flag.

Enum.description: Flash access cycle auto-tuning Enabled
Flash access cycle auto-tuning Disabled

BitField.name: KPKEY0
BitField.description:
KPROM KEY0 Data (Write Only)
Write KPKEY0 data to this register before KEY Comparison operation.

BitField.name: KPKEY1
BitField.description:
KPROM KEY1 Data (Write Only)
Write KPKEY1 data to this register before KEY Comparison operation.

BitField.name: KPKEY2
BitField.description:
KPROM KEY2 Data (Write Only)
Write KPKEY2 data to this register before KEY Comparison operation.

Register.name: FMC_KPKEYTRG
Register.description: KPROM KEY Comparison Trigger Control Register

BitField.name: KPKEYGO
BitField.description:
KPROM KEY Comparison Start Trigger (Write Protect)
Write 1 to start KEY comparison operation and this bit will be cleared to 0 by hardware automatically when KEY comparison operation is finished. This trigger operation is valid while FORBID (FMC_KPKEYSTS [3]) is 0.
Note: This bit is write-protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: KEY comparison operation is finished
KEY comparison is progressed

BitField.name: TCEN
BitField.description:
Timeout Counting Enable Bit (Write Protect)
10 minutes is at least for timeout, and average is about 20 minutes.
Note: This bit is write-protected. Refer to the SYS_REGLCTL register.

Enum.description: Timeout counting Disabled
Timeout counting Enabled if input key is matched after key comparison finished

BitField.name: KEYBUSY
BitField.description: KEY Comparison Busy (Read Only)

Enum.description: KEY comparison is finished
KEY comparison is busy

BitField.name: KEYLOCK
BitField.description:
KEY LOCK Flag
This bit is set to 1 if KEYMATCH (FMC_KPKEYSTS [2]) is 0 and cleared to 0 if KEYMATCH is 1 in Security Key protection. After Mass Erase operation, users must reset or power on /off to clear this bit to 0. This bit also can be set to 1 while:
CPU write 1 to KEYLOCK(FMC_KPKEYSTS[1]) or
KEYFLAG(FMC_KPKEYSTS[4]) is 1 at power-on or reset or
KEYENROM is programmed a non-0xFF value or
Timeout event or
FORBID(FMC_KPKEYSTS[3]) is 1
CONFIG write protect is depended on CFGFLAG

Enum.description: KPROM, LDROM and APROM (not include Data Flash) is not in write protection
KPROM, LDROM and APROM (not include Data Flash) is in write protection

BitField.name: KEYMATCH
BitField.description:
KEY Match Flag (Read Only)
This bit is set to 1 after KEY comparison complete if the KEY0, KEY1 and KEY2 are matched with the 96-bit security keys in KPROM; and cleared to 0 if KEYs are unmatched. This bit is also cleared to 0 while
CPU writing 1 to KEYLOCK(FMC_KPKEYSTS[1]) or
Timeout event or
KPROM is erased or
KEYENROM is programmed to a non-0xFF value.
Chip is in Power-down mode.

Enum.description: KEY0, KEY1, and KEY2 are unmatched with the KPROM setting
KEY0, KEY1, and KEY2 are matched with the KPROM setting

BitField.name: FORBID
BitField.description:
KEY Comparison Forbidden Flag (Read Only)
This bit is set to 1 when KPKECNT(FMC_KPKEY0[4:0]) is more than KPKEMAX (FMC_KPKEY0[12:8]) or KPCNT (FMC_KPCNT [2:0]) is more than KPMAX (FMC_KPCNT [10:8]).

Enum.description: KEY comparison is not forbidden
KEY comparison is forbidden, KEYGO (FMC_KEYTRG [0]) cannot trigger

BitField.name: KEYFLAG
BitField.description:
KEY Protection Enable Flag (Read Only)
This bit is set while the KEYENROM [7:0] is not 0xFF at power-on or reset. This bit is cleared to 0 by hardware while KPROM is erased. This bit is set to 1 by hardware while KEYENROM is programmed to a non-0xFF value.

Enum.description: Security Key protection Disabled
Security Key protection Enabled

BitField.name: CFGFLAG
BitField.description:
CONFIG Write-protection Enable Flag (Read Only)
This bit is set while the KEYENROM [0] is 0 at power-on or reset. This bit is cleared to 0 by hardware while KPROM is erased. This bit is set to 1 by hardware while KEYENROM[0] is programmed to 0.

Enum.description: CONFIG write-protection Disabled
CONFIG write-protection Enabled

BitField.name: KPKECNT
BitField.description:
Error Key Entry Counter at Each Power-on (Read Only)
KPKECNT is increased when entry keys is wrong in Security Key protection. KPKECNT is cleared to 0 if key comparison is matched or system power-on.

BitField.name: KPKEMAX
BitField.description:
Maximum Number for Error Key Entry at Each Power-on (Read Only)
KPKEMAX is the maximum error key entry number at each power-on. When KPKEMAXROM of KPROM is erased or programmed, KPKEMAX will also be updated. KPKEMAX is used to limit KPKECNT(FMC_KPKEY0[5:0]) maximum counting. The FORBID (FMC_KPKEYSTS [3]) will be set to 1 when KPKECNT is more than KPKEMAX.

BitField.name: KPCNT
BitField.description:
Power-on Counter for Error Key Entry (Read Only)
KPCNT is the power-on counting for error key entry in Security Key protection. KPCNT is cleared to 0 if key comparison is matched.

BitField.name: KPMAX
BitField.description:
Power-on Maximum Number for Error Key Entry (Read Only)
KPMAX is the power-on maximum number for error key entry. When KPMAXROM of KPROM is erased or programmed, KPMAX will also be updated. KPMAX is used to limit KPCNT (FMC_KPCNT [3:0]) maximum counting. The FORBID(FMC_KPKEYSTS[3]) will be set to 1 when KPCNT is more than KPMAX

Register.name: PA_DINOFF
Register.description: PA Digital Input Path Disable Control

BitField.name: DINOFF0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit
Each of these bits is used to control if the digital input path of corresponding Px.n pin is disabled. If input is analog signal, users can disable Px.n digital input path to avoid input current leakage.

Enum.description: Px.n digital input path Enabled
Px.n digital input path Disabled (digital input tied to low)

BitField.name: DBEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Input Signal De-bounce Enable Bit
The DBEN[n] bit is used to enable the de-bounce function for each corresponding bit. If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the interrupt. The de-bounce clock source is controlled by DBCLKSRC (GPIO_DBCTL [4]), one de-bounce sample cycle period is controlled by DBCLKSEL (GPIO_DBCTL [3:0]).

Enum.description: Px.n de-bounce function Disabled
Px.n de-bounce function Enabled

BitField.name: DBEN1
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Input Signal De-bounce Enable Bit
The DBEN[n] bit is used to enable the de-bounce function for each corresponding bit. If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the interrupt. The de-bounce clock source is controlled by DBCLKSRC (GPIO_DBCTL [4]), one de-bounce sample cycle period is controlled by DBCLKSEL (GPIO_DBCTL [3:0]).

Enum.description: Px.n de-bounce function Disabled
Px.n de-bounce function Enabled

BitField.name: TYPE0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Edge or Level Detection Interrupt Trigger Type Control
TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is used to control the triggered interrupt is by level trigger or by edge trigger. If the interrupt is by edge trigger, the trigger source can be controlled by de-bounce. If the interrupt is by level trigger, the input source is sampled by one HCLK clock and generates the interrupt.

Enum.description: Edge trigger interrupt
Level trigger interrupt

BitField.name: FLIEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Falling Edge or Low Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

Enum.description: Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Disabled
Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Enabled

The RHIEN (Px_INTEN[n+16]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the RHIEN (Px_INTEN[n+16]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at high level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from low to high.

Enum.description: Px.n level high or low to high interrupt Disabled
Px.n level high or low to high interrupt Enabled

Register.name: PB_DINOFF
Register.description: PB Digital Input Path Disable Control

BitField.name: DINOFF0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit
Each of these bits is used to control if the digital input path of corresponding Px.n pin is disabled. If input is analog signal, users can disable Px.n digital input path to avoid input current leakage.

Enum.description: Px.n digital input path Enabled
Px.n digital input path Disabled (digital input tied to low)

BitField.name: DATMSK0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Data Output Write Mask
These bits are used to protect the corresponding DOUT (Px_DOUT[n]) bit. When the DATMSK (Px_DATMSK[n]) bit is set to 1, the corresponding DOUT (Px_DOUT[n]) bit is protected. If the write signal is masked, writing data to the protect bit is ignored.

Enum.description: Corresponding DOUT (Px_DOUT[n]) bit can be updated

BitField.name: DBEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Input Signal De-bounce Enable Bit
The DBEN[n] bit is used to enable the de-bounce function for each corresponding bit. If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the interrupt. The de-bounce clock source is controlled by DBCLKSRC (GPIO_DBCTL [4]), one de-bounce sample cycle period is controlled by DBCLKSEL (GPIO_DBCTL [3:0]).

Enum.description: Px.n de-bounce function Disabled
Px.n de-bounce function Enabled

BitField.name: TYPE0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Edge or Level Detection Interrupt Trigger Type Control
TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is used to control the triggered interrupt is by level trigger or by edge trigger. If the interrupt is by edge trigger, the trigger source can be controlled by de-bounce. If the interrupt is by level trigger, the input source is sampled by one HCLK clock and generates the interrupt.

Enum.description: Edge trigger interrupt
Level trigger interrupt

BitField.name: FLIEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Falling Edge or Low Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

Enum.description: Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Disabled
Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Enabled

Port A-H Pin[n] Falling Edge or Low Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

Enum.description: Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Disabled
Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Enabled

Register.name: PC_DINOFF
Register.description: PC Digital Input Path Disable Control

BitField.name: DINOFF0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit
Each of these bits is used to control if the digital input path of corresponding Px.n pin is disabled. If input is analog signal, users can disable Px.n digital input path to avoid input current leakage.

Enum.description: Px.n digital input path Enabled
Px.n digital input path Disabled (digital input tied to low)

BitField.name: DBEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Input Signal De-bounce Enable Bit
The DBEN[n] bit is used to enable the de-bounce function for each corresponding bit. If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the interrupt. The de-bounce clock source is controlled by DBCLKSRC (GPIO_DBCTL [4]), one de-bounce sample cycle period is controlled by DBCLKSEL (GPIO_DBCTL [3:0]).

Enum.description: Px.n de-bounce function Disabled
Px.n de-bounce function Enabled

BitField.name: TYPE0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Edge or Level Detection Interrupt Trigger Type Control
TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is used to control the triggered interrupt is by level trigger or by edge trigger. If the interrupt is by edge trigger, the trigger source can be controlled by de-bounce. If the interrupt is by level trigger, the input source is sampled by one HCLK clock and generates the interrupt.

Enum.description: Edge trigger interrupt
Level trigger interrupt

BitField.name: FLIEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Falling Edge or Low Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

Enum.description: Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Disabled
Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Enabled

When setting the RHIEN (Px_INTEN[n+16]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at high level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from low to high.

Enum.description: Px.n level high or low to high interrupt Disabled
Px.n level high or low to high interrupt Enabled

Register.name: PD_DINOFF
Register.description: PD Digital Input Path Disable Control

BitField.name: DINOFF0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit
Each of these bits is used to control if the digital input path of corresponding Px.n pin is disabled. If input is analog signal, users can disable Px.n digital input path to avoid input current leakage.

Enum.description: Px.n digital input path Enabled
Px.n digital input path Disabled (digital input tied to low)

BitField.name: DINOFF1
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit

BitField.name: DBEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Input Signal De-bounce Enable Bit
The DBEN[n] bit is used to enable the de-bounce function for each corresponding bit. If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the interrupt. The de-bounce clock source is controlled by DBCLKSRC (GPIO_DBCTL [4]), one de-bounce sample cycle period is controlled by DBCLKSEL (GPIO_DBCTL [3:0]).

Enum.description: Px.n de-bounce function Disabled
Px.n de-bounce function Enabled

BitField.name: TYPE0
BitField.description:

TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is used to control the triggered interrupt is by level trigger or by edge trigger. If the interrupt is by edge trigger, the trigger source can be controlled by de-bounce. If the interrupt is by level trigger, the input source is sampled by one HCLK clock and generates the interrupt.

BitField.name: FLIEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Falling Edge or Low Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

Enum.description: Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Disabled
Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Enabled

BitField.name: RHIEN1
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Rising Edge or High Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The RHIEN (Px_INTEN[n+16]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the RHIEN (Px_INTEN[n+16]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at high level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from low to high.

Enum.description: Px.n level high or low to high interrupt Disabled

Register.name: PE_DINOFF
Register.description: PE Digital Input Path Disable Control

BitField.name: DINOFF0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit
Each of these bits is used to control if the digital input path of corresponding Px.n pin is disabled. If input is analog signal, users can disable Px.n digital input path to avoid input current leakage.

Enum.description: Px.n digital input path Enabled
Px.n digital input path Disabled (digital input tied to low)

BitField.name: DATMSK0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Data Output Write Mask
These bits are used to protect the corresponding DOUT (Px_DOUT[n]) bit. When the DATMSK (Px_DATMSK[n]) bit is set to 1, the corresponding DOUT (Px_DOUT[n]) bit is protected. If the write signal is masked, writing data to the protect bit is ignored.

Enum.description: Corresponding DOUT (Px_DOUT[n]) bit can be updated

BitField.name: DBEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Input Signal De-bounce Enable Bit
The DBEN[n] bit is used to enable the de-bounce function for each corresponding bit. If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the interrupt. The de-bounce clock source is controlled by DBCLKSRC (GPIO_DBCTL [4]), one de-bounce sample cycle period is controlled by DBCLKSEL (GPIO_DBCTL [3:0]).

Enum.description: Px.n de-bounce function Disabled
Px.n de-bounce function Enabled

BitField.name: TYPE0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Edge or Level Detection Interrupt Trigger Type Control
TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is used to control the triggered interrupt is by level trigger or by edge trigger. If the interrupt is by edge trigger, the trigger source can be controlled by de-bounce. If the interrupt is by level trigger, the input source is sampled by one HCLK clock and generates the interrupt.

Enum.description: Edge trigger interrupt
Level trigger interrupt

BitField.name: FLIEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Falling Edge or Low Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

Enum.description: Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Disabled
Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Enabled

Register.name: PF_DINOFF
Register.description: PF Digital Input Path Disable Control

BitField.name: DINOFF0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit
Each of these bits is used to control if the digital input path of corresponding Px.n pin is disabled. If input is analog signal, users can disable Px.n digital input path to avoid input current leakage.

Enum.description: Px.n digital input path Enabled
Px.n digital input path Disabled (digital input tied to low)

BitField.name: DBEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Input Signal De-bounce Enable Bit
The DBEN[n] bit is used to enable the de-bounce function for each corresponding bit. If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the interrupt. The de-bounce clock source is controlled by DBCLKSRC (GPIO_DBCTL [4]), one de-bounce sample cycle period is controlled by DBCLKSEL (GPIO_DBCTL [3:0]).

Enum.description: Px.n de-bounce function Disabled
Px.n de-bounce function Enabled

BitField.name: TYPE0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Edge or Level Detection Interrupt Trigger Type Control
TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is used to control the triggered interrupt is by level trigger or by edge trigger. If the interrupt is by edge trigger, the trigger source can be controlled by de-bounce. If the interrupt is by level trigger, the input source is sampled by one HCLK clock and generates the interrupt.

Enum.description: Edge trigger interrupt
Level trigger interrupt

BitField.name: FLIEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Falling Edge or Low Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

Enum.description: Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Disabled
Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Enabled

Enum.description: Px.n level high or low to high interrupt Disabled
Px.n level high or low to high interrupt Enabled

BitField.name: RHIEN13
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Rising Edge or High Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The RHIEN (Px_INTEN[n+16]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the RHIEN (Px_INTEN[n+16]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at high level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from low to high.

Enum.description: Px.n level high or low to high interrupt Disabled

Register.name: PG_DINOFF
Register.description: PG Digital Input Path Disable Control

BitField.name: DINOFF0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit
Each of these bits is used to control if the digital input path of corresponding Px.n pin is disabled. If input is analog signal, users can disable Px.n digital input path to avoid input current leakage.

Enum.description: Px.n digital input path Enabled
Px.n digital input path Disabled (digital input tied to low)

BitField.name: DINOFF1
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit
Each of these bits is used to control if the digital input path of corresponding Px.n pin is disabled. If input is analog signal, users can disable Px.n digital input path to avoid input current leakage.

Enum.description: Px.n digital input path Enabled
Px.n digital input path Disabled (digital input tied to low)

BitField.name: DINOFF2
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit
Each of these bits is used to control if the digital input path of corresponding Px.n pin is disabled. If input is analog signal, users can disable Px.n digital input path to avoid input current leakage.

Px.n digital input path Disabled (digital input tied to low)

BitField.name: DBEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Input Signal De-bounce Enable Bit
The DBEN[n] bit is used to enable the de-bounce function for each corresponding bit. If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the interrupt. The de-bounce clock source is controlled by DBCLKSRC (GPIO_DBCTL [4]), one de-bounce sample cycle period is controlled by DBCLKSEL (GPIO_DBCTL [3:0]).

Enum.description: Px.n de-bounce function Disabled
Px.n de-bounce function Enabled

BitField.name: TYPE0

Port A-H Pin[n] Edge or Level Detection Interrupt Trigger Type Control
TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is used to control the triggered interrupt is by level trigger or by edge trigger. If the interrupt is by edge trigger, the trigger source can be controlled by de-bounce. If the interrupt is by level trigger, the input source is sampled by one HCLK clock and generates the interrupt.

BitField.name: FLIEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Falling Edge or Low Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

Enum.description: Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Disabled
Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Enabled

If the interrupt is edge trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from low to high.

Register.name: PH_DINOFF
Register.description: PH Digital Input Path Disable Control

BitField.name: DINOFF0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Digital Input Path Disable Bit
Each of these bits is used to control if the digital input path of corresponding Px.n pin is disabled. If input is analog signal, users can disable Px.n digital input path to avoid input current leakage.

Enum.description: Px.n digital input path Enabled
Px.n digital input path Disabled (digital input tied to low)

BitField.name: DATMSK0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Data Output Write Mask
These bits are used to protect the corresponding DOUT (Px_DOUT[n]) bit. When the DATMSK (Px_DATMSK[n]) bit is set to 1, the corresponding DOUT (Px_DOUT[n]) bit is protected. If the write signal is masked, writing data to the protect bit is ignored.

Enum.description: Corresponding DOUT (Px_DOUT[n]) bit can be updated

BitField.name: DBEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Input Signal De-bounce Enable Bit
The DBEN[n] bit is used to enable the de-bounce function for each corresponding bit. If the input signal pulse width cannot be sampled by continuous two de-bounce sample cycle, the input signal transition is seen as the signal bounce and will not trigger the interrupt. The de-bounce clock source is controlled by DBCLKSRC (GPIO_DBCTL [4]), one de-bounce sample cycle period is controlled by DBCLKSEL (GPIO_DBCTL [3:0]).

Enum.description: Px.n de-bounce function Disabled
Px.n de-bounce function Enabled

BitField.name: TYPE0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Edge or Level Detection Interrupt Trigger Type Control
TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is used to control the triggered interrupt is by level trigger or by edge trigger. If the interrupt is by edge trigger, the trigger source can be controlled by de-bounce. If the interrupt is by level trigger, the input source is sampled by one HCLK clock and generates the interrupt.

Enum.description: Edge trigger interrupt
Level trigger interrupt

BitField.name: FLIEN0
BitField.description:
Port A-H Pin[n] Falling Edge or Low Level Interrupt Trigger Type Enable Bit
The FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit is used to enable the interrupt for each of the corresponding input Px.n pin. Set bit to 1 also enable the pin wake-up function.
When setting the FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

Enum.description: Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Disabled
Px.n level low or high to low interrupt Enabled

When setting the FLIEN (Px_INTEN[n]) bit to 1 :
If the interrupt is level trigger (TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 1), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state is at low level.
If the interrupt is edge trigger(TYPE (Px_INTTYPE[n]) bit is set to 0), the input Px.n pin will generate the interrupt while this pin state changed from high to low.

BitField.name: CURADDR
BitField.description:
PDMA Current Description Address (Read Only)
This field indicates a 32-bit current external description address of PDMA controller.
Note: This field is read only and used for Scatter-Gather mode only to indicate the current external description address.

This field indicates a 32-bit current external description address of PDMA controller.
Note: This field is read only and used for Scatter-Gather mode only to indicate the current external description address.

Register.name: PDMA_DSCT0_CTL
Register.description: Descriptor Table Control Register of PDMA Channel n

BitField.name: OPMODE
BitField.description:
PDMA Operation Mode Selection
Note: Before filling new transfer task in the Descriptor Table, user must check the PDMA_INTSTS[1] to make sure the curren task is complete.

Enum.description: Idle state: Channel is stopped or this table is complete, when PDMA finish channel table task, OPMODE will be cleared to idle state automatically
Basic mode: The descriptor table only has one task. When this task is finished, the PDMA_INTSTS[1] will be asserted

Scatter-Gather mode: When operating in this mode, user must give the next descriptor table address in PDMA_DSCT_NEXT register; PDMA controller will ignore this task, then load the next task to execute

BitField.name: TXTYPE
BitField.description: Transfer Type

Enum.description: Burst transfer type
Single transfer type

BitField.name: BURSIZE
BitField.description:
Burst Size
Note: This field is only useful in burst transfer type.

Enum.description: 128 Transfers
64 Transfers
32 Transfers
16 Transfers
8 Transfers
4 Transfers
2 Transfers
1 Transfers

BitField.name: TBINTDIS
BitField.description:
Table Interrupt Disable Bit
This field can be used to decide whether to enable table interrupt or not. If the TBINTDIS bit is enabled it will not generates TDIFn(PDMA_TDSTS[15:0]) when PDMA controller finishes transfer task.
Note: This function only for scatter-gather mode.

Enum.description: Table interrupt Enabled
Table interrupt Disabled

BitField.name: SAINC
BitField.description:
Source Address Increment
This field is used to set the source address increment size.
Note: The fixed address function is not supported in memory to memory transfer type.

Enum.description: No increment (fixed address)

BitField.name: DAINC
BitField.description:
Destination Address Increment
This field is used to set the destination address increment size.
Note: The fixed address function is not supported in memory to memory transfer type.

Enum.description: No increment (fixed address)

BitField.name: TXWIDTH
BitField.description:
Transfer Width Selection
This field is used for transfer width.
Note: The PDMA transfer source address (PDMA_DSCT_SA) and PDMA transfer destination address (PDMA_DSCT_DA) should be alignment under the TXWIDTH selection

Enum.description: One byte (8 bit) is transferred for every operation
One half-word (16 bit) is transferred for every operation
One word (32-bit) is transferred for every operation

BitField.name: STRIDEEN
BitField.description: Stride Mode Enable Bit

Enum.description: Stride transfer mode Disabled
Stride transfer mode Enabled

BitField.name: TXCNT
BitField.description:
Transfer Count
The TXCNT represents the required number of PDMA transfer, the real transfer count is (TXCNT + 1); The maximum transfer count is 65536, every transfer may be byte, half-word or word that is dependent on TXWIDTH field.
Note: When PDMA finish each transfer data, this field will be decrease immediately.

PDMA Operation Mode Selection
Note: Before filling new transfer task in the Descriptor Table, user must check the PDMA_INTSTS[1] to make sure the curren task is complete.

Enum.description: Idle state: Channel is stopped or this table is complete, when PDMA finish channel table task, OPMODE will be cleared to idle state automatically
Basic mode: The descriptor table only has one task. When this task is finished, the PDMA_INTSTS[1] will be asserted

Scatter-Gather mode: When operating in this mode, user must give the next descriptor table address in PDMA_DSCT_NEXT register; PDMA controller will ignore this task, then load the next task to execute

BitField.name: TXTYPE
BitField.description: Transfer Type

Enum.description: Burst transfer type
Single transfer type

BitField.name: BURSIZE
BitField.description:
Burst Size
Note: This field is only useful in burst transfer type.

Enum.description: 128 Transfers
64 Transfers
32 Transfers
16 Transfers
8 Transfers
4 Transfers
2 Transfers
1 Transfers

BitField.name: TBINTDIS
BitField.description:
Table Interrupt Disable Bit
This field can be used to decide whether to enable table interrupt or not. If the TBINTDIS bit is enabled it will not generates TDIFn(PDMA_TDSTS[15:0]) when PDMA controller finishes transfer task.
Note: This function only for scatter-gather mode.

Enum.description: Table interrupt Enabled
Table interrupt Disabled

BitField.name: SAINC
BitField.description:
Source Address Increment
This field is used to set the source address increment size.
Note: The fixed address function is not supported in memory to memory transfer type.

Enum.description: No increment (fixed address)

BitField.name: DAINC
BitField.description:
Destination Address Increment
This field is used to set the destination address increment size.
Note: The fixed address function is not supported in memory to memory transfer type.

Enum.description: No increment (fixed address)

BitField.name: TXWIDTH
BitField.description:
Transfer Width Selection
This field is used for transfer width.
Note: The PDMA transfer source address (PDMA_DSCT_SA) and PDMA transfer destination address (PDMA_DSCT_DA) should be alignment under the TXWIDTH selection

Enum.description: One byte (8 bit) is transferred for every operation
One half-word (16 bit) is transferred for every operation
One word (32-bit) is transferred for every operation

BitField.name: STRIDEEN
BitField.description: Stride Mode Enable Bit

Enum.description: Stride transfer mode Disabled
Stride transfer mode Enabled

BitField.name: TXCNT
BitField.description:
Transfer Count
The TXCNT represents the required number of PDMA transfer, the real transfer count is (TXCNT + 1); The maximum transfer count is 65536, every transfer may be byte, half-word or word that is dependent on TXWIDTH field.
Note: When PDMA finish each transfer data, this field will be decrease immediately.

Register.name: PDMA_DSCT0_NEXT
Register.description: Next Scatter-gather Descriptor Table Offset Address of PDMA Channel n

BitField.name: NEXT
BitField.description:
PDMA Next Descriptor Table Offset
This field indicates the offset of the next descriptor table address in system memory.
Write Operation:
If the system memory based address is 0x2000_0000 (PDMA_SCATBA), and the next descriptor table is start from 0x2000_0100, then this field must fill in 0x0100.
Read Operation:
When operating in scatter-gather mode, the last two bits NEXT[1:0] will become reserved, and indicate the first next address of system memory.
Note 1: The descriptor table address must be word boundary.
Note 2: Before filled transfer task in the descriptor table, user must check if the descriptor table is complete.

BitField.name: EXENEXT
BitField.description:
PDMA Execution Next Descriptor Table Offset
This field indicates the offset of next descriptor table address of current execution descriptor table in system memory.
Note: write operation is useless in this field.
